A hypercovering in a site is a generalization of a covering, see
\cite[Expos\'e V, Sec. 7]{SGA4}. Given a hypercovering $K$ of an object
$X$, there is a {\v C}ech to cohomology spectral sequence
expressing the cohomology of an abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}$
over $X$ in terms of the cohomology of the sheaf over the
components $K_n$ of $K$. It turns out that there are always
enough hypercoverings, so that taking the colimit over all hypercoverings,
the spectral sequence degenerates and the cohomology of $\mathcal{F}$
over $X$ is computed by the colimit of the {\v C}ech cohomology groups.

source_scope_events_unadjudicated.text_excerpt: Let us first unwind Definition \ref{definition-SR}. An object of $\text{SR}(X_{Zar}, X)$ is simply given by a set $I$ and for each $i \in I$ an open $U_i \subset X$. Let us denote this by $\{U_i\}_{i \in I}$ since there can be no confusion about the morphism $U_i \to X$. A morphism $\{U_i\}_{i \in I} \to \{V_j\}_{j \in J}$ between two such objects is given by a map of sets $\alpha : I \to J$ such that $U_i \subset V_{\alpha(i)}$ for all $i \in I$. When is such a morphism a covering? This is the case if and only if for every $j \in J$ we have $V_j = \bigcup_{i\in I, \ \alpha(i) = j} U_i$ (and is a covering in the site $X_{Zar}$).
